proposals.before: Reform the harem: fix precedence so favorites cannot monopolize favor or breed arrogance; check the chaos of Bao Si and Zhao Feiyan; let humble consorts rise in due order, each to her station, to widen the chance of heirs and still the jealousies sung in the "White Flowers"; enrich in-laws with gold but bar them from office like the royal fathers of old, and clip the power of consort clans—when the inner quarters are ordered, the realm does not fall into chaos.
proposals.after: Reform the harem: fix precedence so favorites cannot monopolize favor or breed arrogance; check the chaos of Bao Si and Lady Yan; let humble consorts rise in due order, each to her station, to widen the chance of heirs and still the jealousies sung in the "White Flowers"; enrich in-laws with gold but bar them from office like the royal fathers of old, and clip the power of consort clans—when the inner quarters are ordered, the realm does not fall into chaos.
proposals.reason: Chinese 褒、閻 refers to Bao Si and Lady Yan (閻) from the preceding exempla, not Zhao Feiyan.

proposals.before: Labor day and night in the stern virtue of yiyin day: keep your charge, aid the throne, punish evil without sparing kin, promote good without shunning enemies—only thus can you show perfect fairness and win trust across the realm.
proposals.after: Labor day and night in the stern virtue of Yi Yin: keep your charge, aid the throne, punish evil without sparing kin, promote good without shunning enemies—only thus can you show perfect fairness and win trust across the realm.
proposals.reason: Chinese 伊尹 is the minister Yi Yin; 'yiyin day' is a corrupted rendering of that name.

proposals.before: You ought morning and night be diligent, grasp yiyin day's strong virtue, thereby to guard duty and correct the ruler, punish wickedness without shrinking from kin and loved ones, raise good without shrinking from foes and enemies, thereby to display utmost fairness, establish trust in the four directions.
proposals.after: You ought morning and night be diligent, grasp Yi Yin's strong virtue, thereby to guard duty and correct the ruler, punish wickedness without shrinking from kin and loved ones, raise good without shrinking from foes and enemies, thereby to display utmost fairness, establish trust in the four directions.
proposals.reason: Chinese 伊尹之強德 is Yi Yin's strong virtue; 'yiyin day' is corrupt.

proposals.before: Gu Yong's learning was broad but shallow compared with Du Qin, Du Ye, or the depth of Liu Xiang and his son and Yang Xiong.
proposals.after: Gu Yong's learning in the classics was broad but rough, roughly equal to Du Qin and Du Ye, and not as thorough as Liu Xiang and his son and Yang Xiong.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 'shallow compared with Du Qin, Du Ye, or the depth of Liu Xiang...' misstates 略等 (roughly equal) as inferiority to Du Qin and Du Ye.

proposals.before: When Han first rose, Empress Dowager Lü wielded power for her private relatives and also made a maternal grandson the successor to Emperor Xiaohui. At that time the line of succession was unclear and all affairs were largely dark; changes such as daytime gloom and thunder in winter were too many to record.
proposals.after: When Han first rose, Empress Dowager Lü wielded power for her private relatives and also made a maternal grandson the empress of Emperor Xiaohui. At that time the line of succession was unclear and all affairs were largely dark; changes such as daytime gloom and thunder in winter were too many to record.
proposals.reason: Chinese 以外孫為孝惠後 means making a maternal grandson Empress Xiaohui’s empress (後), not the successor to Emperor Xiaohui.

proposals.before: His son Du Lin loved antiquity and had talent; under Guangwu he rose to Grand Minister of Works.
proposals.after: Ye’s son Lin was quiet and fond of antiquity, and also had refined talent; during Jianwu he passed through the ranked ministers to Grand Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents “under Guangwu”; Chinese only has reign-period 建武中 and should remain Jianwu without adding an unstated personal name.

proposals.before: Gu Yong's "three-seven" warning was true loyalty; yet he cited Shen Bo to flatter Wang Feng, sowed strife with Ping'e, and read Venus and Mars to suit his patrons—candor thin, words many.
proposals.after: Gu Yong’s “three-seven” warning was true loyalty; yet he cited Shen Bo to flatter Wang Feng, sowed strife with Ping’a, and read Venus and Mars to suit his patrons—candor thin, words many.
proposals.reason: 平阿 is Ping’a elsewhere in this chapter; idiomatic Ping’e is a wrong transliteration of the same title.

decisions.reason: 褒、閻 names Bao and Yan; Zhao Feiyan (趙飛燕) is not in the Chinese and invents the wrong consort.
伊尹 is the Shang minister Yi Yin; “yiyin day” is a corrupted misreading of that personal name.
伊尹之強德 is Yi Yin’s strong virtue; the literal “yiyin day” is the same name corruption.

decisions.after: Gu Yong's learning in the classics was broad but superficial, roughly equal to that of Du Qin and Du Ye, though not as thorough as that of Liu Xiang and his son or Yang Xiong.
decisions.reason: 與杜欽、杜鄴略等 means roughly equal to Du Qin and Du Ye; the original wrongly ranks Yong beneath them.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 與杜欽、杜鄴略等，不能洽浹如劉向父子及揚雄也

decisions.reason: The text uses 後 in the sense of dynastic successor: Empress Dowager Lu made a maternal grandson Emperor Hui's successor. A male maternal grandson cannot be his empress, and the following sentence explicitly discusses the unclear succession.

decisions.after: His son Du Lin was quiet, fond of antiquity, and endowed with refined talent. During Jianwu, he served successively among the ranked ministers and rose to Grand Minister of Works.
decisions.reason: Chinese has 建武中 only, with 清靜好古 and 歷位列卿; “under Guangwu” invents an unstated personal name and drops those details.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 鄴於林，清靜好古，亦有雅材，建武中歷位列卿，至大司空

decisions.after: Gu Yong's "three-seven" warning was true loyalty; yet he cited Shen Bo to flatter Wang Feng, sowed strife with Ping'a, and read Venus and Mars to suit his patrons—candor thin, words many.
decisions.reason: 平阿 is the title Ping’a; Ping’e is a wrong transliteration of the same two graphs.
